title_en: Seth Green’s Star Wars: Detours Will Finally See the Light of Day
summary_en: A selection of episodes from Seth Green’s animated Star Wars sitcom will be exhibited at the soon-to-open Lucas Museum.
body_en:
Seth Green’s long-shelved animated Star Wars sitcom Star Wars: Detours will finally find itself in front of the public, albeit as an exhibit at George Lucas’ soon-to-open Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, California. The news comes via an announcement from Green himself during a panel discussion on the museum at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, as reported by Entertainment Weekly.
“We made a show with George, an animated series,” said Green. “He wanted to make Simpsons in the Star Wars universe. It’s called Detours, and there’s… going to be a curation of episodes from that show on display for the public in the theater.”
Star Wars Detours was officially announced way back at Star Wars Celebration in 2012, although Lucas and Green were broadly discussing the project in public as early as 2010. A variety of clips were showcased around its 2012 reveal, but the series was shelved in the aftermath of Disney’s acquisition of Lucasfilm the same year and its been missing in action ever since.
Green discussed the status of Star Wars Detours with IGN in late 2013 at New York Comic-Con, confirming the crew had 39 episodes completed before the show was frozen in carbonite.
The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art is set to open on September 22. Two theaters (the Robert Flaherty Theater and the Slavko Vorkapich Theater) will showcase curated film selections throughout the day for patrons to drop in and drop out of during their visit.
